sec: Patient Instructions, Myxedema Coma & SREAT / Hashimoto Encephalopathy

items.q: What specific administration instructions must be given to patients taking oral L-thyroxine on page 909?
opts: Take on an empty stomach in the morning (7 - 7:30 am) with a glass of water, and wait 30 minutes before meals
Take with a full meal at dinner time to maximize lipid-phase absorption
Take at bedtime co-administered with calcium and iron supplements
Take dissolved in hot milk twice daily after meals
items.exp: Instructions: 'Empty stomach (morning 7-7:30 am) with glass of water. Take meal after 30 minutes'. (Book p909)

items.q: Match the drug that inhibits L-thyroxine absorption to its formulation — 1) FeSO4 2) CaCO3 3) Al(OH)3 / Sucralfate … A) Ferrous sulfate iron salt B) Calcium carbonate C) Aluminum hydroxide antacid / mucosal protectant
items.exp: Drugs to be avoided because they inhibit absorption include FeSO4, CaCO3, Al(OH)3, and Sucralfate. (Book p909)

items.q: The single most common (m/c) cause of treatment failure in hypothyroid patients prescribed L-thyroxine is ___.
items.exp: Under follow-up: 'm/c cause of treatment failure : Non-compliance'. (Book p909)

items.q: How long after the serum TSH value normalizes does the patient typically achieve clinical symptomatic relief?
items.exp: Page 909 explicitly notes: 'Clinical relief : 3-6 months after TSH value becomes normal'. (Book p909)

items.q: What is the mortality rate of myxedema coma reported on page 909?
items.exp: Under Emergency Conditions: 'myxedema coma : mortality 40%'. (Book p909)

items.q: What are the primary trigger factors listed for precipitating myxedema coma?
opts: Non-compliance and infection (e.g., COVID-19 or lower respiratory tract infection - LRI)
Excessive dietary iodine and strenuous physical exertion
items.exp: Trigger factors for myxedema coma: 'Non-compliance, infection (i.e. covid, LRI)'. (Book p909)

items.q: Match the characteristic 'Hypo' presenting features of myxedema coma — 1) Respiratory 2) Glucose metabolism 3) Electrolytes 4) Body temperature … A) Hypoventilation B) Hypoglycemia C) Hyponatremia D) Hypothermia
items.exp: The 'Hypo' tetrad of myxedema coma consists of Hypoventilation, Hypoglycemia, Hyponatremia, and Hypothermia. (Book p909)

items.q: An elderly woman with myxedema coma is admitted with severe bradycardia, hypothermia (34°C), and low-voltage ECG complexes. Which intravenous fluid is indicated, and which must be avoided?
opts: Hypertonic saline indicated; hypotonic saline strictly avoided
Hypotonic saline indicated; hypertonic saline strictly avoided
5% Dextrose in water indicated; hypertonic saline strictly avoided
Albumin colloid indicated; normal saline strictly avoided
items.exp: Treatment specifies: 'Hypertonic saline (Avoid hypotonic saline)'. (Book p909)

items.q: What is the complete medical treatment regimen for myxedema coma on page 909?
opts: IV L-thyroxine 500 µg OD -> 50-100 µg/day, Steroid, IV T3 5-20 µg, Hypertonic saline
Oral PTU 1000 mg stat, Propranolol 60 mg Q4H, Iopanoic acid, Normal saline
External active warming with heated blankets, Hydrocortisone, Hypotonic saline
IV Levothyroxine 25 µg daily, Furosemide infusion, Potassium chloride
items.exp: Treatment for myxedema coma: IV L-thyroxine 500 µg OD -> 50-100 µg/day, Steroid, IV T3 5-20 µg, and Hypertonic saline. (Book p909)

items.q: Steroid-responsive encephalopathy associated with autoimmune thyroid illness (SREAT / Hashimoto encephalopathy) is an autoimmune vasculitis that is ___ to thyroid function, and can be seen in ___ status.
items.exp: SREAT: 'Can be seen in euthyroid status' and is an 'Autoimmune vasculitis unrelated to thyroid function'. (Book p909)

items.q: Which autoantibody and HLA allele are characteristically elevated and associated with SREAT on page 909?
items.exp: SREAT is characterized by '↑↑ Antibodies (Anti-enolase Ab)' and 'HLA -B8'. (Book p909)

items.q: Match the clinical presentations of SREAT — 1) Progressive cognitive decline 2) Paroxysmal motor events 3) Vascular mimic … A) Altered level of consciousness B) Seizure & myoclonus C) Stroke-like presentation
items.exp: Presentations of SREAT include: slowly progressive cognitive decline (altered level of consciousness), seizure & myoclonus, and stroke-like presentation. (Book p909)

items.q: Assess SREAT management on page 909: I The primary and definitive pharmacologic management is corticosteroids (steroids). II Patients must immediately receive high-dose intravenous levothyroxine.
opts: I is true; II is false
Both I and II are true
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Management of SREAT is explicitly stated as 'management : Steroids'. Thyroid hormone therapy is not the primary treatment since SREAT is vasculitic and unrelated to thyroid function. (Book p909)
